questions_and_answers.question_text: What kind of adverb is běnlái, and where must it go?
What are the two main uses of běnlái?
Which word often follows běnlái in the second use?
Which word is a běnlái clause often related to?
Give two translations for the second use.
Write the Chinese for "Originally I wasn't going to go, but now I will."

answers.answer_text: Wǒ běnlái bú qù, xiànzài qù le.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "I wasn't going to go there in the first place."
Write the Chinese for "Coffee is supposed to be black!"

answers.answer_text: Kāfēi ma, běnlái jiù shi hēide.
It must never come after the verb — it always precedes the verb.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "I never did like her, and I still don't like her."

answers.answer_text: Wǒ běnlái jiù bù xǐhuan ta, xiànzài hái bù xǐhuan ta.

articles.text:
9. Běnlái tāde Zhōngwén bú cuò,      Originally, his Chinese was pretty good,
   líkāi Zhōngguo jiǔle, wàngle      but he's been away from China for a
   hěn duō.                          long time and has forgotten a lot.

Notes on No. 9

běnlái: "originally, in the beginning, at first; to begin with, in the first place." This is a MOVEABLE ADVERB — it may come before or after the subject, but ALWAYS BEFORE THE VERB.

Běnlái has TWO MAIN USES:

(1) SITUATION HAS CHANGED — the situation was originally one way but then it changed.

Wǒ běnlái bú qù, xiànzài qù le.  Originally I wasn't going to go, but
                                 now I will.
Wǒ běnlái bù xǐhuan ta, kěshi    Originally I didn't like her, but now
xiànzài xǐhuan ta le.            I do.
Běnlái wǒ jīntian yào qù         Originally I was going to Guǎngzhōu
Guǎngzhōu, kěshi tiānqì bù hǎo.  today, but the weather is bad.

(2) SITUATION WAS LIKE THIS TO START WITH AND STILL IS — translations include "to begin with" and "in the first place." In this use, běnlái is OFTEN FOLLOWED BY JIÙ.

Wǒ běnlái jiù bù xǐhuan ta,      I never did like her, and I still don't
xiànzài hái bù xǐhuan ta.        like her.
A: Nǐ bié qù nèige dìfang!       Don't go there!
B: Wǒ běnlái jiù bú qù.          I wasn't going to go there in the first
                                 place.
A: Zhèige kāfēi zěnme zhème hēi? Why is this coffee so black?
B: Kāfēi ma, běnlái jiù shi      Coffee is supposed to be black!
hēide.

A clause with běnlái is often related to another with DĀNGRÁN:

Zhèige dōngxi běnlái jiù shi     This thing belongs to you; of course I
nǐde, wǒ dāngrán yào huán gěi    would return it to you.
ni!
